elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to an Affiliate.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits either Party, including PB as Customer, to assign the Agreement in its entirety to an Affiliate without the other Party's prior consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits assignment to a successor in connection with a qualifying transfer, expressly including a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits assignment to a successor through a sale of stock or other transfer of all or substantially all relevant business or assets, covering a qualifying acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 expressly permits assignment to a successor in connection with a sale or transfer of all or substantially all business or assets to which the Agreement relates.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 allows SFJ to assign without PB's consent to any SFJ Affiliate or qualifying successor.

elements.element: Customer consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause requires consent for non-exempt assignments but contains no requirement that PB act reasonably in withholding consent.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor restriction appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The prohibition applies only if the successor assumes PB's obligations. It therefore does not establish an unconditional prohibition, and the retained following sentence still contemplates SFJ terminating pursuant to Section 14.2.6.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits PB to assign the Agreement to a qualifying successor without SFJ's prior consent.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 contains no assignment-notice duty. Section 14.2.6 requires notice of entering a definitive change-of-control agreement, not notice of every successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 mutually permits either Party, including SFJ, to assign to a qualifying successor without consent.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No operative provision requires SFJ to provide written notice of a successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor consent to Customer's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: SFJ's consent is required for non-exempt PB assignments, but no reasonableness standard applies.

elements.element: Customer consent to Vendor's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: PB's consent is required for non-exempt SFJ assignments, but no reasonableness standard applies.

result.reason: Neither level is complete. The preferred position fails because Vendor retains consent-free Affiliate and successor assignment rights, no reasonableness or competitor protections are added, and the change-of-control termination prohibition is conditional. The fallback fails because successor-assignment notices and mutual reasonableness standards are absent. The retained termination-payment sentence creates ambiguity after removal of the express termination grant, and Section 15.6 remains syntactically incomplete by ending with “and.”
